They are not being lazy or careless now; they are trying to prove to themselves and to you that they are not someone who ships bad work. The triple-checking is self-protection dressed up as diligence, and the slowdown is the cost. Underneath it is a real question: do I still belong in this role, or did that one mistake define me here.", "pull": {"collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Quietly absorb the slowdown, say nothing, and hope confidence comes back on its own, which leaves them stuck in the loop with no signal that you still trust them and no way to recalibrate."}, "mentorMove": "Name what you are seeing without judgment, separate the mistake from their competence, and give them a concrete structure for checking work so the decision of when to ship is no longer just their nerves against a blank deadline.", "holdFirm": ["Work still needs to move at a pace the team and customers can rely on.", "Catching mistakes is a skill they need to build, not a fear they need to run from."], "stayFlexible": ["How they build that checking process, whether that is a personal checklist, a peer review step, or a quick sync with you before a handoff.", "The timeline for getting back to full velocity, which can be a ramp rather than an immediate flip."], "forceLevel": {"level": 2, "label": "Questions"}, "script": [{"phase": "Connection", "words": "I have been watching how you have been working since the customer issue, and I want to talk through it with you, just the two of us, because I think there is something worth naming."}, {"phase": "Curiosity", "words": "When you are sitting with a piece of work right now, what does it feel like before you send it? I am asking because I want to understand where your head is, not because anything is wrong."}, {"phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I think is happening. You are spending more energy on the checking than on the work itself, and that is actually the fear driving, not your judgment. Let us build you a short, concrete process you can trust and then stop at, so you are not just checking until the anxiety drops."}, {"phase": "Commitment", "words": "One customer catch is not a verdict on your ability. I am holding you to good work and a sustainable pace because I have seen what you can do and I am not revising that opinion based on one miss. The standard stays up, and I think you can meet it."}], "longGame": "The goal is helping them internalize a calibrated process for quality rather than an emotional one, so that over time their confidence is grounded in a repeatable skill rather than in the absence of mistakes. People who can ship well and recover cleanly from errors become the ones others rely on; people who only feel safe when they are certain tend to stall exactly when the team needs speed."}
situation: A junior shipped something with a mistake a customer caught, and now they are triple-checking everything and velocity has cratered.
